title: Compatible homotopy equivalences are invertible in an enriched pullback along a local fibration
statement: Use simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A small simplicial category has a set of objects, simplicial mapping sets, and associative unital simplicial composition. Its category $\pi_0$ has components of mapping sets as morphisms. Let $p:A\to B$ and $q:C\to B$ be simplicial functors, and assume that $A(a,a')\to B(pa,pa')$ is a Kan fibration for every pair $a,a'$. Form the strict pullback simplicial category $E=A\times_B C$: objects are pairs $(a,c)$ with $pa=qc$, and mapping sets are the corresponding strict pullbacks of mapping simplicial sets. A vertex $u$ in a mapping set of $E$ is invertible in $\pi_0E$ if and only if its projections are invertible in $\pi_0A$ and $\pi_0C$. No mapping set is assumed Kan, and neither functor is assumed to lift equivalences on objects.

Agent formulation of that implicit step; its mapping-space proof uses the right proper Kan model structure, rather than the global Bergner structure. Read online; not archived. proof.text: Write $u:x\to y$ for the given vertex of $E$. If $[u]$ has a two-sided inverse in $\pi_0E$, apply each projection functor to its two inverse equations. Projections preserve composition and identity vertices by the strict pullback definition, so both projected classes are invertible.

source.place: Proposition 2.5, printed p. 8, pullback E before applying Lemma 2.4; agent expansion of the implicit equivalence check, using only Kan--Quillen model axioms and right properness.

proof.text: Assume conversely that the two projections of $u$ are invertible. First, in any simplicial category $D$, a vertex $e:d\to d^\prime$ invertible in $\pi_0D$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $e^*:D(d^\prime,t)\to D(d,t)$ for every object $t$. Indeed choose a vertex $f:d^\prime\to d$ representing the inverse class. The equalities $[fe]=[1_d]$ and $[ef]=[1_{d^\prime}]$ are witnessed by finite zigzags of edges. Composing each such edge with the variable arrow gives a simplicial homotopy between the corresponding self-maps of the mapping simplicial set. Finite-product preservation of realization in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies the realized cylinders with the topological cylinders, so these zigzags realize to homotopies. Thus $|f^*|$ and $|e^*|$ are homotopy inverse maps. By [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change], a homotopy equivalence induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups at every basepoint (the basepoint paths are supplied by the homotopies, which need not be stationary); this is the weak-equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply this to $u_A$, $u_C$, and their common image $u_B$ (the last is invertible because a functor preserves the inverse equations).

source.place: Proposition 2.5, printed p. 8, pullback E before applying Lemma 2.4; agent expansion of the implicit equivalence check, using only Kan--Quillen model axioms and right properness.

proof.text: Here is the fixed-base calculation needed for the mapping pullbacks. Suppose $r:X\to Y$ is a weak equivalence over a simplicial set $Z$, and $X\to Z$ and $Y\to Z$ are Kan fibrations. Factor its graph $X\xrightarrow{(1,r)}X\times_ZY$ as a trivial cofibration $j:X\to M$ followed by a fibration $(s,t):M\to X\times_ZY$, using the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Both projections $X\times_ZY\to X,Y$ are fibrations: a horn lifting problem for either projection is exactly a horn problem for the other original leg. Their composites $s,t$ are fibrations, by successive lifting. As $sj=1_X$ and $tj=r$, two-out-of-three makes both $s$ and $t$ weak equivalences, hence trivial fibrations. For any $T\to Z$, their base changes $s_T,t_T$ are still trivial fibrations, since boundary lifting is preserved by pullback. Also $s_Tj_T=1$, so two-out-of-three gives that $j_T$ and $r_T=t_Tj_T$ are weak equivalences. This is an explicit factorization calculation, with no fibrancy assumption on $Z,X,Y,T$.

source.place: Proposition 2.5, printed p. 8, pullback E before applying Lemma 2.4; agent expansion of the implicit equivalence check, using only Kan--Quillen model axioms and right properness.

proof.text: Now let $X_i\xrightarrow{f_i}Z_i\xleftarrow{g_i}Y_i$, $i=0,1$, be strictly commuting cospans with $f_i$ Kan fibrations, and let $a:X_0\to X_1$, $b:Z_0\to Z_1$, $c:Y_0\to Y_1$ be a commuting map of cospans whose three components are weak equivalences. Put $T=X_1\times_{Z_1}Z_0$. Its projection to $X_1$ is a weak equivalence by right properness of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], applied to $b$ and $f_1$. Thus the map $h=(a,f_0):X_0\to T$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Both $X_0\to Z_0$ and $T\to Z_0$ are fibrations, so the preceding fixed-base calculation, base changed along $g_0$, makes $X_0\times_{Z_0}Y_0\to T\times_{Z_0}Y_0=X_1\times_{Z_1}Y_0$ a weak equivalence. Finally $X_1\times_{Z_1}Y_0\to X_1\times_{Z_1}Y_1$ is the pullback of $c$ along the fibration $X_1\times_{Z_1}Y_1\to Y_1$, so right properness makes it a weak equivalence too. Their composite is the induced map of pullbacks. All pullback identifications here send a compatible tuple to the same coordinates; thus no choice or extra homotopy compatibility is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.5, printed p. 8, pullback E before applying Lemma 2.4; agent expansion of the implicit equivalence check, using only Kan--Quillen model axioms and right properness.

proof.text: For an arbitrary object $z=(a_z,c_z)$ of $E$, apply the preceding calculation to the cospans $A(a_y,a_z)\to B(pa_y,pa_z)\leftarrow C(c_y,c_z)$ and $A(a_x,a_z)\to B(pa_x,pa_z)\leftarrow C(c_x,c_z)$. Their left legs are Kan fibrations by the hypothesis on $p$. Precomposition with $u_A,u_B,u_C$ gives a strictly commuting map of these cospans, since $p,q$ preserve composition and $p(u_A)=q(u_C)$ as vertices. All three maps are weak equivalences by Step 2. Their strict pullbacks are exactly $E(y,z)$ and $E(x,z)$. Consequently $u^*:E(y,z)\to E(x,z)$ is a weak equivalence and induces a bijection on components. This uses the general cospan calculation just proved, rather than the homotopy-pullback assertion for Kan complexes; no mapping set has been assumed Kan.

source.place: Proposition 2.5, printed p. 8, pullback E before applying Lemma 2.4; agent expansion of the implicit equivalence check, using only Kan--Quillen model axioms and right properness.

proof.text: Take $z=x$ in Step 5. Surjectivity on components supplies a vertex $v:y\to x$ with $[vu]=[1_x]$. Take $z=y$. Under the injective map $\pi_0E(y,y)\to\pi_0E(x,y)$, the two classes $[uv]$ and $[1_y]$ have equal images: $[(uv)u]=[u(vu)]=[u]=[1_yu]$. Hence $[uv]=[1_y]$. Thus $[v]$ is a two-sided inverse of $[u]$; together with Step 1 this proves the assertion, with no equivalence-lifting condition on the object maps.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_pullback_equivalence {A B C : SCat.{u}} (p : A ⟶ B) (q : C ⟶ B) (_hp : ∀ a a' : A, SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.J.rlp (p.map a a')) (E : PullbackCone p q) (_hE : IsLimit E) {x y : E.pt} (e : (EnrichedCategory.Hom x y) _⦋0⦌) : (∃ d : (EnrichedCategory.Hom y x) _⦋0⦌, π₀.mk ((eComp SSet x y x).app _ (e, d)) = π₀.mk ((eId SSet x).app _ PUnit.unit) ∧ π₀.mk ((eComp SSet y x y).app _ (d, e)) = π₀.mk ((eId SSet y).app _ PUnit.unit)) ↔ (∃ d : (EnrichedCategory.Hom (E.fst.obj y) (E.fst.obj x)) _⦋0⦌, π₀.mk ((eComp SSet (E.fst.obj x) (E.fst.obj y) (E.fst.obj x)).app _ ((E.fst.map x y).app _ e, d)) = π₀.mk ((eId SSet (E.fst.obj x)).app _ PUnit.unit) ∧ π₀.mk ((eComp SSet (E.fst.obj y) (E.fst.obj x) (E.fst.obj y)).app _ (d, (E.fst.map x y).app _ e)) = π₀.mk ((eId SSet (E.fst.obj y)).app _ PUnit.unit)) ∧ (∃ d : (EnrichedCategory.Hom (E.snd.obj y) (E.snd.obj x)) _⦋0⦌, π₀.mk ((eComp SSet (E.snd.obj x) (E.snd.obj y) (E.snd.obj x)).app _ ((E.snd.map x y).app _ e, d)) = π₀.mk ((eId SSet (E.snd.obj x)).app _ PUnit.unit) ∧ π₀.mk ((eComp SSet (E.snd.obj y) (E.snd.obj x) (E.snd.obj y)).app _ (d, (E.snd.map x y).app _ e)) = π₀.mk ((eId SSet (E.snd.obj y)).app _ PUnit.unit))
lean.note: The strict enriched pullback is represented by a PullbackCone with IsLimit in the recorded ordinary category SCat of simplicial categories and arbitrary-object enriched functors. Two-sided inverses are expanded directly in the recorded component quotient; no local Kan or equivalence-lifting assumptions are added.
